audit.recode_to: conflict (stress tradition: dynamic accent predominantly on 2nd syllable, verbs initial — Talibov 2001:421, Schulze 1997:22, Ibragimov 1990; vs. Kodzasov 1990:344 'словесное ударение отсутствует', 4 syllabic/moraic tones contrastive on the first two syllables). If the catalog prefers to keep a stress code pending Elementy 1999, downgrade fixed-strict -> fixed-dominant (2nd syllable; Talibov 'преимущественно', initial stress in verbs per Schulze) and add Kodzasov 1990 to 'contra'.
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding quotations (Schulze 1997:22 §2.1.5; Talibov 2001:421 §2.1.2) confirmed verbatim in held page images. (2) Deciding sources are two sketches (1997, 2001). They do not themselves support 'strict': Talibov says stress falls 'predominantly' on the 2nd syllable and can be initial (óхьанас, óкIанас); Schulze says verbs are always initial-stressed and CVC/CVRC monosyllabic nouns keep stem stress before suffixes. (3) downloaded now from the official MSU Kibrik site: Kibrik & Kodzasov 1990, where the phonetician Kodzasov, from fieldwork with an accentuated dictionary, states for Tsakhur (Mikik) 'word stress is absent' and describes four syllabic tones (H 137, L 33, R 26, F 11 monosyllables) contrastive only on the first two syllables (p.344), listing Tsakhur among the syllabic-tone languages of Daghestan (p.318). Schulze 1997 fn.33 knows of and rejects functional tone b
audit.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again: both verbatim, re-read from page images. (1) Talibov 2001:421 §2.1.2, 'Для Ц. я. характерно силовое ударение, которое падает преимущественно на второй слог от начала слова (хьунáшше…, гынéй…, аккá…). Ударным может быть и первый слог (óхьанас 'есть', óкIанас 'писать'). Многосложные слова … дополнительное ударение, ср. хьéтIалас 'звать', где основное ударение падает на долгий е, а дополнительное – на а второго слога.' Same page §2.1.3 adds 'Наблюдается редукция гласных в безударной позиции (гней < гыней)'. (2) Schulze 1997:22 §2.1.5
